newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union urges Lufthansa to new pay talks.
newsitem.headline: German union urges Lufthansa to new pay talks.

text.p: German trade union DAG said on Friday it was calling for "the immediate resumption of constructive talks" with Lufthansa AG over the ongoing wage dispute with the German airline.

The statement follows the results of a strike ballot on Wednesday in which Lufthansa pilots gave formal approval to union leaders to call a strike if the German airline did not improve its current contract offer.

Lack of participation by flight attendants and ground workers in the six-week balloting period meant, however, that the union failed to reach the quorum needed to give approval for them to participate in any strike action.
"Securing Lufthansa jobs against further transfer (of activities) abroad must be a central theme of the talks," DAG said in a statement following a meeting of its main wage committee in Frankfurt.
Lufthansa said it had no comment to make on the statement.

Following the ballot results earlier this week, Lufthansa said it saw no current strike threat and itself called on the DAG to return to talks since it said an "overwhelming majority" of its 58,000 workers were against a strike.
But the airline reaffirmed that it would not change its current offer, which is based on a deal struck late last year with members of the OeTV public sector and transport union.

The 27-month deal by the OeTV, which represents mainly ground workers, offers a 1.8 percent wage increase in 1998, a one-time payment of one-third of a month's salary and a 500 mark share of last year's profit in cash or Lufthansa stock.

DAG in its statement reiterated its fears that a 27-month contract would leave its members with little recourse if Lufthansa then decided to transfer activities to subsidiary companies operating under less favourable working conditions.

DAG and Lufthansa were also scheduled to meet in Hamburg on Friday to discuss the airline's current restructuring programme. Sources close to the talks said the wage conflict would also likely be discussed.
